notes: be given is read as the frame carried by the written tehi (rules 20, 21) rather than as a supplied lexical verb; the Hebrew writes a verb here, so rule 20's added-verb clause does not reach it. Head stays on be, the token realizing haya's own lexeme (rule 24).
The suffix on maskurtekh is realized by the dative thee in the ASV's recasting (rule 18).
under whose wings divides as in v. 2: tahat keeps its own under, and whose is the one word carrying relative and resumptive possessive suffix together (rule 22).
